note: Documented spread, unauthorised releases and contamination incidents, past and present, as map points. This is a hand-compiled record: the GM Contamination Register logged 396 incidents across 63 countries between 1997 and 2013 and then stopped, and nothing has replaced it, so there is no feed to harvest. Twenty-five incidents. Each entry below is an incident that was found and reported. Coordinates are the place the material was found, at region or district level, so every record is precise:false. Dates are the year the incident became public, which is usually later than the year it happened.

projects.name: Glyphosate-resistant creeping bentgrass — spread into wild Agrostis
projects.type: Grass, transgene escape into wild relatives
projects.size: Established in wild populations across multiple counties
projects.desc: WHAT. Creeping bentgrass engineered to survive glyphosate, grown in trials for the golf-course market, moved out of its test plots into resident populations of wild Agrostis species. WHERE IT SITS. The strongest documented case of transgene spread into wild plant communities anywhere — from a crop that was never commercialised. WHY IT MATTERS. The source fields were taken out of production and a mitigation programme was run. Three years later surveyors pulled 585 plants and 62 in every hundred were still resistant; the published conclusion was that eradication was not realistic. The grass is outcrossing, wind-pollinated and perennial, a risk profile most assessment work had not been done on.

projects.name: GloFish — fluorescent transgenic fish established in Brazilian streams
projects.type: Ornamental fish, escape into wild waters
projects.size: Multiple streams in the Atlantic Forest region
projects.desc: WHAT. Fluorescent transgenic zebrafish, sold as aquarium pets since 2003, spread from ornamental fish farms and established breeding populations in Atlantic Forest streams. WHERE IT SITS. The pet trade as a release pathway — no biosafety application, no assessment, no monitoring. WHY IT MATTERS. This is the quietest large-scale release of engineered animals that has happened. Millions have been sold as decoration for two decades, and the spread route was a fish farm rather than a laboratory. The organisms are now reproducing in a biodiversity hotspot, and no regulator anywhere treated the ornamental trade as a release pathway before it happened.

projects.name: StarLink maize — unapproved variety in the human food supply
projects.type: Maize, unapproved variety in food
projects.size: Estimated 300+ recalled food products
projects.desc: WHAT. A maize variety approved only for animal feed, on allergenicity concerns, was found in taco shells and hundreds of other human foods. WHERE IT SITS. The first mass recall caused by segregation failure between an approved and an unapproved use of the same crop. WHY IT MATTERS. It established that split approvals do not survive contact with a commodity grain system: once a crop enters bulk handling, feed and food are the same stream. Residues turned up in testing for years after the variety was withdrawn, and the episode is why almost no regulator grants feed-only approvals for a bulk commodity any more.

projects.name: LLRICE 601 — unapproved rice in the US commercial supply
projects.type: Rice, unapproved variety in commerce
projects.state: Arkansas and the US rice belt
projects.size: US rice exports; EU and Japan import suspensions
projects.desc: WHAT. A herbicide-tolerant rice line that had never been commercialised was found in the US long-grain commercial supply and in exports. WHERE IT SITS. Rice accounted for roughly a third of all incidents in the GM Contamination Register despite no GM rice being grown commercially anywhere. WHY IT MATTERS. The line had last been field-tested years earlier. Trial material persisted, moved into commercial seed stocks, and closed export markets; US farmers won substantial settlements. It is the clearest demonstration that a field trial is not a contained event, and that the containment period assumed by an assessment is not the period over which material actually persists.

projects.name: Triffid flax — deregistered line found in exports a decade later
projects.type: Flax, deregistered variety in exports
projects.size: Canadian flax exports to the EU
projects.desc: WHAT. A herbicide-tolerant flax deregistered and supposedly removed from the seed system in 2001 turned up in Canadian exports to Europe in 2009. WHERE IT SITS. A case where the withdrawal was voluntary, thorough on paper, and insufficient. WHY IT MATTERS. Eight years after a line was pulled and its seed stocks destroyed, it was still in the commercial system. Deregistration is not removal. Canada's flax export market to Europe took years to rebuild, and the cost fell on farmers who had never grown the variety.

projects.name: Transgenes in Mexican maize landraces
projects.type: Maize, transgene presence in landraces
projects.size: Multiple communities across several states
projects.desc: WHAT. Transgenic sequences were found in native maize landraces in Oaxaca, in a country where GM maize planting was prohibited. The first 2001 paper was heavily contested and partly repudiated; later independent surveys confirmed transgene presence. WHERE IT SITS. Inside the centre of origin and diversity for maize — the reservoir every commercial maize variety on Earth was ultimately bred from. WHY IT MATTERS. This is not contamination of a crop but of the source of the crop, held for generations by communities who licensed nothing and were asked nothing. There is no procedure for taking it back out and no agency anywhere with a mandate to try. It is the reason Mexico moved its prohibition into the Constitution in 2025.

projects.name: Feral herbicide-tolerant canola with stacked traits, roadsides
projects.type: Canola, feral populations with stacked traits
projects.size: Roadside populations across the state
projects.desc: WHAT. Surveys along North Dakota roadsides found feral canola carrying herbicide-tolerance traits, including plants with traits from two separate commercial events stacked together. WHERE IT SITS. Outside any field, outside any permit, reproducing on its own. WHY IT MATTERS. The stacked plants had not been bred by anyone. Feral populations were crossing with each other in the ditches, which means the material that spread was not merely persisting but recombining. Comparable feral populations have been documented along transport routes in Japan around ports that import canola but do not grow it.

projects.name: Jacobina — engineered mosquito genome entering the wild population
projects.type: Mosquito, introgression from release strain
projects.size: 27 months of weekly releases, ~450,000 males per week
projects.desc: WHAT. After 27 months of weekly releases of self-limiting engineered male Aedes aegypti, genotyping across more than 21,000 markers found DNA from the release strain in the wild population. WHERE IT SITS. The most advanced commercial open-release programme for engineered animals in the world. WHY IT MATTERS. What moved was the release strain's background genome rather than the self-limiting transgene, and the company disputes the paper's framing. But the design premise had been that lethality was complete and the target population's genetics would be unaffected. Laboratory work had already shown a few per cent of offspring surviving. Self-limiting was a design claim, and the field tested it.

projects.name: Bt10 maize — wrong unapproved line shipped for four years
projects.type: Maize, unapproved line distributed in error
projects.state: United States (exports to EU and Japan)
projects.size: Estimated tens of thousands of tonnes
projects.desc: WHAT. An unapproved maize line was distributed and exported for four years in the belief that it was a different, approved line. The error was disclosed only after it had been found. WHERE IT SITS. A failure of internal identification rather than of containment. WHY IT MATTERS. The company could not tell its own lines apart for four years, across commercial distribution and international export. Every argument about traceability, identity preservation and event-specific detection assumes the developer knows which event it is shipping.

projects.name: Unapproved herbicide-tolerant cotton planted at scale
projects.type: Cotton, unapproved trait planted commercially
projects.size: Estimated millions of hectares
projects.desc: WHAT. Herbicide-tolerant cotton that has never been approved in India has been planted across large areas for years, supplied through an unlicensed seed trade. WHERE IT SITS. The world's largest cotton-growing country, with an approval system the planting simply bypassed. WHY IT MATTERS. India's first Bt cotton was likewise found growing in Gujarat before any approval existed, and the pattern has repeated with every trait since. Where a trait is commercially attractive and enforcement is thin, approval becomes optional — which makes a register a record of what was asked for rather than of what is in the ground.

projects.name: Bt63 rice — unapproved GM rice in food products and exports
projects.type: Rice, unapproved variety in food chain
projects.size: Detected in exports to Europe over many years
projects.desc: WHAT. An insect-resistant rice line approved only for research was found being grown commercially and turning up in rice products exported to Europe, with detections recurring over more than a decade. WHERE IT SITS. The world's largest rice producer, and a crop eaten directly rather than processed. WHY IT MATTERS. The line spread from research plots into commercial cultivation through informal seed exchange, which is how most seed moves in most of the world. Detections continued long after the authorities acted, and Europe imposed testing requirements on Chinese rice imports that lasted years.

projects.name: GM petunias — engineered ornamentals found in worldwide commerce
projects.type: Ornamental plant, unapproved variety in trade
projects.size: Dozens of varieties across many countries
projects.desc: WHAT. Orange petunias sold in garden centres worldwide were found to contain a maize gene introduced in research decades earlier. Nobody had applied for approval anywhere, and no breeder appeared to know. WHERE IT SITS. The ornamental horticulture trade, which sits outside almost every biosafety monitoring system. WHY IT MATTERS. Engineered plants had been propagated, bred into new varieties and sold internationally for years without anyone noticing, because nobody was looking at flowers. It was found by accident, by a researcher who happened to be curious about the colour. That is the detection system this industry actually has for anything outside a monitored crop.

projects.name: Roundup Ready wheat — unapproved wheat in an Oregon field
projects.type: Wheat, unapproved line found volunteering
projects.size: Export suspensions by Japan and South Korea
projects.desc: WHAT. Glyphosate-tolerant wheat, field-tested years earlier and never commercialised, was found growing as volunteers in an Oregon field. Japan and South Korea suspended US wheat imports. WHERE IT SITS. A crop the industry had deliberately left alone because it is eaten directly and export markets resisted it. WHY IT MATTERS. The investigation never established how the wheat got there. Trial material from a programme that had been discontinued turned up in a commercial field years later, closed export markets within days, and the cause remains unexplained. Similar unexplained finds followed in Montana and Washington.

projects.name: GM papaya — unapproved virus-resistant plants in commercial orchards
projects.type: Papaya, unapproved variety in cultivation
projects.size: Orchards across multiple provinces
projects.desc: WHAT. Virus-resistant papaya from a government research station was found growing in commercial orchards in a country that prohibited open cultivation of GM crops. WHERE IT SITS. Drift from a public research programme rather than a company trial. WHY IT MATTERS. Seed was distributed from the station to farmers, apparently informally, and spread from there. It is a reminder that the containment question is not only about corporate applicants: a public institution with a research permit is subject to the same failure modes, and in this case the state was both the source of the spread and the authority investigating it.

projects.name: Herbicide-tolerant bentgrass — second spread via seed movement
projects.type: Grass, secondary spread beyond control area
projects.state: Malheur County, Oregon and into Idaho
projects.status: Spread beyond the designated control area
projects.size: Irrigation canals and adjacent land in two states
projects.desc: WHAT. Resistant creeping bentgrass spread beyond the state-designated control area, moving along irrigation canals into neighbouring counties and across a state line. WHERE IT SITS. The same spread as the Jefferson County case, years later and further out. WHY IT MATTERS. Water moved it. Containment plans written around pollen distance and buffer zones did not account for a stoloniferous perennial travelling along irrigation infrastructure, and by the time it was found the affected area was no longer the one being managed. The regulator eventually deregulated the crop rather than continuing to pursue eradication.

projects.name: Bt cotton found growing before any approval existed
projects.type: Cotton, unapproved trait in commercial fields
projects.size: Estimated tens of thousands of hectares before approval
projects.desc: WHAT. Insect-resistant cotton was found growing across Gujarat before India had approved any GM crop. The regulator ordered the crop destroyed; farmers resisted, and the trait was approved commercially the following year. WHERE IT SITS. The founding case of Indian agricultural biotechnology, and the template for everything since. WHY IT MATTERS. Approval followed adoption rather than preceding it. Once a trait is already in the ground at scale, an approval decision becomes a decision about whether to criminalise existing farmers, which is not the decision the framework was designed to make. The same sequence has repeated with every trait India has argued about since.

projects.name: GM oilseed rape naturalised around import ports
projects.type: Canola, feral populations at import points
projects.size: Roadsides between ports and crushing plants
projects.desc: WHAT. Herbicide-tolerant oilseed rape has established feral populations along the roads between Japanese ports and the plants that crush imported seed, in a country that does not grow the crop commercially. WHERE IT SITS. Drift through transport rather than through cultivation. WHY IT MATTERS. Japan imports engineered canola and grows none, so every one of these plants arrived by falling off a truck. Biosafety assessment concerns itself with what happens in and around a field; it has almost nothing to say about spillage along a haulage route, which is how these populations began and how they continue.

projects.name: Engineered petunias — second wave found after the first recall
projects.type: Ornamental plant, unapproved variety in trade
projects.size: Further varieties on sale years after the first clearance
projects.desc: WHAT. Four years after engineered petunias were withdrawn from sale worldwide, further engineered varieties were found on the market. WHERE IT SITS. The same trade, the same gene, after a supposedly complete clearance. WHY IT MATTERS. The first episode prompted destruction orders across several continents and was treated as resolved. It was not. Ornamental breeding lines are propagated vegetatively and traded informally between breeders, so material persists in a system nobody is monitoring — and it is found only when someone happens to test.

projects.name: Herbicide-tolerant canola in a country that never approved it
projects.type: Canola, unapproved trait in cultivation
projects.size: Certified seed lots and adjacent crops
projects.desc: WHAT. Traces of engineered canola turned up in certified conventional seed lots and in crops grown by farmers who had bought conventional seed. WHERE IT SITS. Inside the seed certification system — the mechanism that is supposed to guarantee what a farmer is buying. WHY IT MATTERS. Coexistence policy assumes a grower can choose. That choice depends on certified seed being what the label says, and certification tolerances are set at a percentage rather than at zero. A farmer who buys conventional seed and grows an engineered crop has not made a choice at all.

projects.name: Engineered wheat found again, years after the first Oregon case
projects.type: Wheat, unapproved line found volunteering
projects.size: Isolated fields; export markets disrupted again
projects.desc: WHAT. Glyphosate-tolerant wheat from discontinued trials was found volunteering in fields in Washington and later Montana, years after the Oregon discovery and in different states. WHERE IT SITS. A crop that was never commercialised, appearing repeatedly, in places with no recorded trial history. WHY IT MATTERS. Three separate finds, in three states, with the cause established in none of them. Each closed export markets within days. Whatever mechanism is moving this material has now operated for over a decade after the programme that created it was shut down, and no investigation has identified it.

projects.name: Farmed salmon genetics established in wild Norwegian rivers
projects.type: Salmon, genetic introgression into wild populations
projects.status: Documented in a majority of assessed rivers
projects.size: Assessed across ~200 wild populations
projects.desc: WHAT. Long-term genetic monitoring has found farmed salmon ancestry in a large majority of assessed wild Norwegian salmon populations, in many of them at levels classed as substantial. WHERE IT SITS. The only systematic river-by-river record of genetic introgression from farmed animals into wild ones anywhere in the world. WHY IT MATTERS. Nothing here was genetically engineered. The genetics are the product of intensive selection for farm conditions, and they entered wild populations through routine spread out of pens over decades. It is the clearest measured example of the process this map argues about for crops, and it exists only because one country chose to fund the monitoring.

projects.name: Atlantic salmon established in Patagonian rivers after farm spread
projects.type: Salmon, introduced species established after spread
projects.size: Multiple river systems; single spread of hundreds of thousands of fish
projects.desc: WHAT. Atlantic salmon, not native to the southern hemisphere, have spread out of Chilean farms in very large numbers — individual incidents have released hundreds of thousands of fish — and now occur in Patagonian rivers. WHERE IT SITS. The world's second-largest salmon farming industry, in a country with no native salmon at all. WHY IT MATTERS. An introduced predatory fish established itself through spread out of pens nobody was required to design for permanence. No biosafety framework was engaged at any point, because nothing was engineered — which is why the containment argument on this map cannot be confined to organisms a statute happens to define.

projects.name: Engineered petunias in a third wave, years after two recalls
projects.type: Ornamental plant, unapproved variety recurring in trade
projects.state: European and North American horticultural trade
projects.size: Varieties still surfacing after two clearance rounds
projects.desc: WHAT. Engineered petunias have surfaced repeatedly in the ornamental trade after clearance operations in 2017 and again in 2021, each treated at the time as complete. WHERE IT SITS. A trade that propagates vegetatively, exchanges material informally between breeders, and sits outside every biosafety monitoring system. WHY IT MATTERS. Two full recalls across several continents did not clear it. The material persists in a system nobody monitors and is found only when somebody happens to test, which makes the recurrence a measure of the monitoring rather than of the plant.

projects.name: Unapproved GM soy planted across Ukraine
projects.type: Soy, unapproved trait in commercial cultivation
projects.size: Estimated a substantial share of the national soy crop
projects.desc: WHAT. Herbicide-tolerant soy has been planted widely in Ukraine for years despite no GM crop being approved for cultivation, supplied through an unlicensed seed trade and detected in exports. WHERE IT SITS. A major grain and oilseed exporter selling into markets with sharply different GM rules. WHY IT MATTERS. This is the fourth case on this map of adoption preceding approval, after India, Brazil and Paraguay. The pattern is consistent enough to be treated as the normal route rather than the exception: where a trait is commercially attractive and enforcement is thin, the register records what was asked for and not what is in the ground.

projects.name: GM maize found growing in Mexico despite the planting prohibition
projects.type: Maize, unapproved cultivation in a centre of origin
projects.size: Detected in commercial fields and in tortilla samples
projects.desc: WHAT. Transgenic maize has been detected growing in Mexican commercial fields and in maize food products, in a country where planting GM maize is prohibited and the prohibition is now constitutional. WHERE IT SITS. Inside the centre of origin and diversity for maize, the crop's global genetic reservoir. WHY IT MATTERS. Imported grain intended for food and feed can be planted, and some of it is. A prohibition on planting does not control seed that arrives as food, which is the gap every import-and-prohibit country on this map has and almost none of them tests for.
